title: SEIS AI Lab engineer robot, body study v002
tagline: An engineer version of the SEIS robot with armoured legs, a connector arm, a wrist display and a red Lato Bold 6. A design study, not a final model.
stats: 230 meshes · 67,496 triangles · 12 materials in the GLB · 24 bones · mouth shape keys Speaking and Emphasis · 6 spool caps · 2.84 m tall with antenna in the source's audit · Blender 5.1.2
description: The second SEIS robot study: the v001 box head, raised eyes, waveform mouth and a bent, broken-mast antenna on a new tapered body with layered chest, narrow upper legs and flared white shin armour, in white, black, gray, Northeastern red and gold accents. The chest 6 is an extruded Lato Bold mesh. The robot's right arm (viewer's left) is a prototype instrument: retained folding fingers, a split palm, a solid audio-style connector with insulating rings, six spool caps and a wrist display with scrolling task text. The source calls it a "visual and mechanical design prototype" and says it is not a functional system. This is a design study, not a final model.

views.title: Three-quarter
views.text: The hero view. It is the v001 box robot with an armoured body bolted on: white shoulder caps and thin gold trim, a shield-shaped chest with the red 6, black waist, white shin armour with red knee panels. Tidy, but the head and attitude still say v001.

views.title: Front
views.text: The wrist display (viewer's left) and the connector below it are the readable story; the left hand on the other side is a small blocky fist. Legs are shorter and boxier than the armoured references.

views.title: Back
views.text: A slotted back panel carried over from v001, red shoulder inserts and square red shin plates. Plain.

views.title: Side
views.text: A thin stack of parts in profile. The chest plate and calibration marks were moved onto their supporting surfaces after the source's side review.

views.title: Top
views.text: Plan view: box head, broad shoulders, display at the side. Only useful for width.

views.title: Silent face
views.text: Mouth shape key off, so no waveform. The antenna is bent at the tip with a second broken mast, as specified.

views.title: Hand mode
views.text: tool_deployed at 0: fingers shown, connector hidden inside the wrist.

views.title: Wrist-reading pose
views.text: Raised elbow and head tilt to read the wrist display, connector retracted. The pose is a rigid-part rotation; it looks stiff.

views.title: Wrist display close-up
views.text: Legible only here: AGENTS / 06 with REVIEW, LISTEN, CHECK, CONNECT, PLAN. The text is flat emissive lettering, schematic status text, not live data.

views.title: Connector deployed
views.text: The solid plug extended with white, black and gold-coloured bands and the six spool caps at the elbow housing. The bands are visual only: no trust, listen or tell logic exists.

views.title: Hand close-up
views.text: Four folding fingers under the display housing. Chunky; the palm split is only a gap, not a mechanism you could mistake for working.

views.title: Wireframe
views.text: Roughly 67,500 triangles across 230 separate parts; every part is fully weighted to one bone.

compares.title: Supplied photograph vs engineer (front)
compares.text: Left: one of the seven supplied photographs of an armoured black-and-gold figure, front. Right: the engineer render. Borrowed loosely: broad shoulder caps, a layered chest, big flared shin armour. Not matched: the photograph's smooth sculpted torso, tapering cone-shaped greaves that reach up to the knee, large gauntlet arms and small head. The render is a boxy white-and-red robot with a very large head and short blocky legs. Likeness to the photograph: weak. It reads as the original SEIS robot with armour added, which is consistent with the v003 README's statement quoted on this page.

compares.title: Supplied photograph vs engineer (back)
compares.text: Left: the back photograph, turned slightly. Right: the engineer back. The photograph has curved shoulder shells, a layered back plate and huge flared boots; the render has a flat slotted panel and straight-sided legs. Different shapes; only the colour accents (red instead of gold) and the idea of a plate across the shoulder blades carry over. Likeness: low.

compares.title: Supplied photograph vs engineer (three-quarter)
compares.text: Left: a supplied photograph from a slight turn. Right: the engineer three-quarter. The poses are close enough to compare. The render's silhouette is a blocky head over a short shield torso; the photograph is a tall, long-legged figure with a small head and sweeping boots. The wrist display and connector have no counterpart in the photographs. Likeness: low.

blend_note: Saved by Blender 5.1.2; it has never been opened in Blender 4.2, so 4.2 compatibility is untested (use Blender 5.1 or later to match the build). The wrist text scrolls through timeline playback and the connector uses Blender drivers; neither carries into the GLB.
glb_note: The GLB uses flat material colours only: no textures or images are embedded (0 textures, 12 materials). It carries the 24-bone skeleton and the Speaking and Emphasis morph targets, in the displayed pose, with no animation clips. Blender drivers and the scrolling display logic are not part of the GLB.

built_by.builder: Codex (OpenAI). Builder identified from Codex session logs on this machine dated 2026-10-18, not from a label in the folder; no product or model version is stated in the files.
built_by.method: Scripted: local Blender Python (scripts/build_engineer.py, assembled from head_helpers.py.txt and body.py.txt); the source says no Blender MCP connection and no paid generation. Recorded checks (reports/CHECKS.md): connector deployment evaluated at 0, .25, .5, .75 and 1; twelve views rendered and inspected; one visible inspect-and-fix pass (the side review moved the chest numeral and leg trim onto their surfaces). No numbered render-versus-reference rounds are logged; the supplied photographs were used for body proportions and armour cues only. The compare images here were made afterwards for this page, by eye.
built_by.tools: Blender 5.1.2 (confirmed by my scene count); Lato Bold font converted to mesh for the 6; the source's own Blender export and re-import check. No game engine import was run.
built_by.date: 2026-10-17 (file times 17:25; the source's CHECKS.md is dated 2026-10-17)
built_by.review: Professor Bear: pending. The source CHECKS.md says: "Ready for design review; this is not human approval of the design." A later source file (the v003 README.txt, in this repository's sibling folder) states: "The previous v002 body was rejected as too similar to the original robot." The files do not say who made that call or when.

limitations: This is a design study, not a final model.
Likeness to the supplied photographs is weak; the body is still close to the original SEIS robot (the v003 README says so in its own words).

The right arm is a visual concept only: cable payout, programmed iris states, quarantine behaviour, live agent connections and voice-driven face animation are not implemented. The wrist display is schematic text, not live agent data.
The source's own prototype proportions are not manufacturing dimensions; the connector travels 0.24 m in the audit.
Rigid FK posing only; no IK, no animation clips in the GLB, no engine import test.

Counts: my count_scene run reports 231 mesh objects and 67,498 triangles, which is the source's 230 meshes and 67,496 triangles plus a 2-triangle floor plane; 13 materials in the .blend against 12 in the GLB.
The 2.84 m height (with antenna) is from the source's own audit; my count cannot give it because of the large floor plane. At this height the robot is large compared with the 1.68 m of v001.
I did not copy the 24 readout frame PNGs or the review.html; the 4-second mp4 is included.
build_notes:
## What it is

A second body for the SEIS robot with an instrument arm, built by `scripts/build_engineer.py`. The supplied pasted design notes (an agent-orchestrating engineer called "Jig", kept in `references/engineer-arm-notes.txt`) were treated as background only: the source says direct requests override conflicting pasted notes, so the model keeps the eyes and waveform and the Northeastern palette, includes wrist text, and does not use the notes' spirit-level face or orange palette.

## What I measured

`scripts/count_scene.py` on the .blend (Blender 5.1.2): 231 mesh objects, 67,498 triangles, 13 materials, 1 armature, 24 bones, 1 camera, 3 lights (`reports/scene-counts-seis_robot_engineer_v002.json`). The floor plane accounts for one mesh and two triangles over the source's 230 meshes and 67,496 triangles.

GLB inspection: 0 images, 0 textures, 12 materials, 1 skin, 0 animations.

## What the source reports (not re-run by me)

- 230 meshes, 67,496 triangles, 24 bones, every vertex weighted to one bone, six spool caps, both mouth morph targets present.
- Connector deployment evaluated at five states: fingers fold first, the palm separates, the plug then travels 0.24 m.
- GLB re-import in Blender matched mesh, triangle and bone counts and dimensions. The first export used the rest pose; setting `export_rest_position_armature=False` corrected it.

## Controls

On `SEIS_Engineer_Rig` (Object Properties, Custom Properties): `tool_deployed` 0 to 1 folds the fingers, separates the palm, then extends the plug; `screen_orient` 0 to 1 turns the display toward its wearer. On `SEIS_Engineer_Waveform_Mouth`: `Speaking` and `Emphasis` shape keys. Play the timeline to scroll the wrist text.

## Notes

Palette from the project's saved Northeastern guidelines: red C8102E, bold gold A4804A, light gold C8A978, cool black 1E2028, grays 49494D and 9B9C9E, white and canvas F6F6F4. Paths in copied scripts and logs were replaced with placeholders; the Lato font path in `build_engineer.py` points outside this repository.

## Not copied

review.html, the 24 readout frame PNGs, `.blend1` backups.
